semantics.clock: All sequential updates occur on positive clk edges, as stated.
semantics.reset: Synchronous active-high reset sets all four digits to zero; reset has priority over counting.
semantics.count: Each non-reset rising edge increments the decimal count by one, carrying from ones to thousands.
semantics.enable: Combinational ena[0] indicates ones=9; ena[1] indicates lower two digits=99; ena[2] indicates lower three digits=999. These indicate upper-digit increments on the upcoming counting edge.
semantics.initialization: No initial state is specified; no initialization is imposed before the first reset edge.

numeric.encoding: q[3:0] ones, q[7:4] tens, q[11:8] hundreds, q[15:12] thousands; each digit 0..9.

verification.oracle: Independent integer decimal counter converted to BCD, based on original problem.
verification.sampling: Check settled outputs after rising edges and combinational enables between edges. Assert reset between edges to verify synchronous behavior.
verification.cases: Reset, consecutive resets, every count over two complete decimal periods, all carry boundaries, and reset during a nonzero count.
verification.termination: Fatal on mismatch, bounded timeout, PASS only after all checks.

specification_ambiguities.topic: Enable bit mapping and reset gating
specification_ambiguities.resolution: Map ena[0], ena[1], ena[2] to digits 1,2,3 respectively. Use lower-digit carry conditions independent of reset, because enable indicates when digits should increment and reset is separately synchronous.
Four decimal digits naturally wrap 9999 to 0000; no overflow port is specified.
Unspecified; verification establishes state with synchronous reset before expecting count values.
